findings.title: No bare-hand contact with RTE food or a pre-approved alternative procedure properly allowed.
findings.comment: An employee was observed using bare hands to handle ready-to-eat (RTE) foods in the additional kitchen space. The items include sliced American cheese and sliced breads. The activity was ceased and corrected. Discussed always using gloves to handles RTE foods and what foods are considered RTE. Bare hands usage should only be used to a minimal if handling raw animal protein or if there is a kill step occurring.  Ensure that bare hands are never used to handle RTE foods to protect against cross contamination of food items.
findings.citation_text: 3-301.11(B) Preventing Contamination from Hands. (B) Except when washing fruits and vegetables as specified under §3-302.15 or as specified in (D) and (E) of this section, FOOD EMPLOYEES may not contact exposed, READY-TO-EAT FOOD with their bare hands and shall use suitable UTENSILS such as deli tissue, spatulas, tongs, single-use gloves, or dispensing EQUIPMENT.

findings.title: Food separated and protected.
findings.comment: There was improper storage order observed inside of the prep cooler placed in the additional kitchen space. There were raw tenderloins observed above RTE foods (sliced cheeses and deli meats). Shown to the PIC and the items were rearranged to correct the violation. Handouts referencing safe storage order in refrigerated units was given to the facility. Ensure that raw animal protein is always stored below all RTE foods to prevent cross contamination.
findings.citation_text: 3-302.11(A)(1) Packaged and Unpackaged Food - Separation, Packaging, and Segregation. (A) FOOD shall be protected from cross contamination by: (1) Except as specified in (1)(d) below or when combined as ingredients, separating raw animal FOODS during storage, preparation, holding, and display from: (a) Raw READY-TO-EAT FOOD including other raw animal FOOD such as FISH for sushi or MOLLUSCAN SHELLFISH, or other raw READY-TOEAT FOOD such as fruits and vegetables, (b) Cooked READY-TO-EAT FOOD, and (c) Fruits and vegetables before they are washed; (d) Frozen, commercially processed and packaged raw animal FOOD may be stored or displayed with or above frozen, commercially processed and packaged, ready-to-eat food.

findings.title: Food-contact surfaces; cleaned and sanitized.
findings.comment: The rubber soda gun holster in the main bar area was observed with dried liquids on the inner surfaces. The surface was shown to the PIC and the holster was cleaned and sanitized during the visit to correct the violation. Ensure that all food contact surfaces of soda guns and gun holsters are cleaned as frequent as often to prevent accumulated debris.
findings.citation_text: 4-601.11(A) Equipment, Food-Contact Surfaces, Nonfood-Contact Surfaces, and Utensils. (A) EQUIPMENT FOOD-CONTACT SURFACES and UTENSILS shall be clean to sight and touch.

findings.title: Proper cooling methods used; adequate equipment for temperature control.
findings.comment: A container of cheese sauce that was recently cooked was in the process of actively being cooled. The employees mentioned that the cheese sauce was placed inside of the cooler 45 minutes prior to the visit. The cheese sauce was probed at 95F and contained a tight fitting lid. Discussed with the employees proper timeframes for safe cooling and approved cooling methods. The facility was instructed to break down cheese sauce into smaller portions, containers that allow heat to transfer easily, and keep the containers uncovered so that heat can escape. A handout referencing proper cooling methods was given the facility. Ensure that TCS are cooled within the proper timeframe of 6 hours, as well use an approved cooling method.
findings.citation_text: 3-501.15(A) Cooling Methods. (A) Cooling shall be accomplished in accordance with the time and temperature criteria specified under § 3-501.14 by using one or more of the following methods based on the type of FOOD being cooled: (1) Placing the food in shallow pans; (2) Separating the food into smaller or thinner portions; (3) Using rapid cooling equipment; (4) Stirring the food in a container placed in an ice water bath; (5) Using containers that facilitate heat transfer; (6) Adding ice as an ingredient; or (7) Other effective methods.

findings.title: Physical facilities installed, maintained, and cleaned.
findings.comment:
The following areas are in need of cleaning:
- The floor and wall around the fryers in the main kitchen contains accumulated grease debris
- The floors and walls underneath and behind pieces of equipment in the additional kitchen space has accumulated debris 
Ensure that these areas are cleaned as frequent as necessary to prevent accumulation.
findings.citation_text: 6-501.12 Cleaning, Frequency and Restrictions. (A) PHYSICAL FACILITIES shall be cleaned as often as necessary to keep them clean. (B) Except for cleaning that is necessary due to a spill or other accident, cleaning shall be done during periods when the least amount of FOOD is exposed such as after closing.

findings.title: Hands clean and properly washed.
findings.comment: An employee was observed washing hands without using a barrier to turn off faucet handles. Discussed with person-in-charge proper handwashing procedures. When washing hands, be sure to educate employees on using barriers to turn off faucet handles to avoid recontaminating freshly washed hands.
findings.citation_text: 2-301.12(C) Cleaning Procedure. (C) To avoid recontaminating their hands or surrogate prosthetic devices, FOOD EMPLOYEES may use disposable paper towels or similar clean barriers when touching surfaces such as manually operated faucet handles on a HANDWASHING SINK or the handle of a restroom door.

findings.title: Food separated and protected.
findings.comment:
There was improper storage order in the following cold holding equipment:
- Raw chicken stored above produce and seafood items in the walk in cooler
- Raw chicken stored above seafood and ready-to-eat foods in the kitchen prep cooler

Items were rearranged to correct the violation. Ensure that chicken is always stored below any RTE foods or foods with lower cooking temperature to prevent cross contamination.
findings.citation_text: 3-302.11(A)(1) Packaged and Unpackaged Food - Separation, Packaging, and Segregation. (A) FOOD shall be protected from cross contamination by: (1) Except as specified in (1)(d) below or when combined as ingredients, separating raw animal FOODS during storage, preparation, holding, and display from: (a) Raw READY-TO-EAT FOOD including other raw animal FOOD such as FISH for sushi or MOLLUSCAN SHELLFISH, or other raw READY-TOEAT FOOD such as fruits and vegetables, (b) Cooked READY-TO-EAT FOOD, and (c) Fruits and vegetables before they are washed; (d) Frozen, commercially processed and packaged raw animal FOOD may be stored or displayed with or above frozen, commercially processed and packaged, ready-to-eat food.

findings.title: Adequate handwashing sinks properly supplied and accessible.
findings.comment: A build up of food debris was observed in the drain of the kitchen hand-sink. Discussed proper usage of hand-sink with PIC to educate employees. Ensure that handwashing sinks are only used for handwashing. Never use hand-sink for rinsing dishes or other food contact surfaces.
findings.citation_text: 5-205.11 Using a Handwashing Sink. (A) A HANDWASHING SINK shall be maintained so that it is accessible at all times for EMPLOYEE use. (B) A HANDWASHING SINK may not be used for purposes other than handwashing. (C) An automatic handwashing facility shall be used in accordance with manufacturer’s instructions.
